method: Real Playwright browser recordings, reviewed in chronological frame contact sheets (3–6fps for illustration changes,2fps for full repeated-film journey) and transition-focused frames. Recordings are compact review encodings only; protected production media are unchanged. Cinema comparison uses direct scene anchors for identical repeat-visit sampling; native-scroll recording separately shows actual wheel/keyboard, loop and history interactions.
findings: Direct pointer/range reveals the same illustrative layer without a flash or touch-target collision.
Capsule SVG images dissolve, while exactly one selected caption is painted; inactive captions do not ghost during the dissolve.
Atlas native enlargement/close retains readable text and restores focus.
Both retained environmental films show distinct advancing frames on repeat visits in before/after recordings; returned forest has no retained duplicate layer.
The context cue is quiet and readable on desktop, hidden on phone.
Any unused black cells in contact sheets are sheet padding after the clip ends, not website frames.
nativeRecordingSetup: The untrimmed native recording starts with the newly opened blank browser during AppKit/setup before the scenario navigation; these initial blank frames are retained, not a flash between movie scenes. First server paint, hydration and delayed decoding are validated separately in the four cold-visit tests of the initial native run.
